importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — basic GI sheet cabin, PUF panel modular home, LGSF villa-style, double-storey unit all look fundamentally different. Buyers use the image to identify structure type and livability standard before reading any text; wrong visual type causes immediate skip.

Configuration (1BHK/2BHK), structure material (MS/GI/LGSF), wall panel type, and floor area are primary shortlisting gates. Without these specs a buyer cannot determine whether the structure meets their residential, labour camp, or institutional requirement.

Per sq ft rate is the universal comparison metric in Indian construction. Buyers actively compare rates across sellers after visual and spec shortlisting; price varies substantially with structure material, insulation grade, and configuration, so it is spec-driven rather than a flat commodity rate.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard portable cabin units (10x12 ft, 10x20 ft) are sometimes quoted per unit by sellers — this creates direct price comparison confusion with per sq ft listings. Unit must be shown alongside price to prevent misreading.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft is the dominant unit but per unit quoting exists for standard cabin sizes; a buyer comparing two listings cannot interpret price without knowing the unit, making this a necessary price qualifier.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Recognised national brands (Tata Nest-In, EPACK Prefab) exist but IndiaMART buyers predominantly search by spec and price; most sellers are regional fabricators and buyers do not search by manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional and government buyers evaluate manufacturer credentials, installation track record, and service network during vendor selection; individual buyers assess seller reliability for a high-value, site-assembled purchase — but specs and price carry greater weight at the shortlisting stage.
